correctness.rationale: For each ordered pair of edge interiors, every nonexceptional pair realizes the ambient sum-product geodesic in the one-skeleton. Exceptional pairs are different layer copies of one geodesic factor edge, where endpoint routing gives D=d_layers+min(s+t,2ell-s-t) and A=d_layers+abs(s-t). Exact triangular-area integration yields (ell-z)_+^2/ell^2; multiplication by ell^2 and b_i(b_i-1) and normalization by Lambda^2 proves the survival law. Tail integration gives all q>0 moments, while jumps of the second derivative recover the positive weighted length multiset. Independent point-to-point Dijkstra and factor-product calculations agree on 138064 finite exact-rational point pairs across 19 products; experiments corroborate but do not prove the theorem. Boundary and geodesicity hypotheses were checked explicitly.

value.rationale: The metric one-skeleton of a graph product is a natural transport network inside a product length space; the geometric gap between permissible one-dimensional routes and ambient sum-metric travel is a substantive invariant. The exact law is topology-independent except for vertex-copy multiplicities, works with arbitrary edge weights and arbitrarily many factors, and has a nontrivial inverse conclusion: knot locations and jump sizes identify an aggregate weighted edge-length spectrum from random route-excess measurements. This is neither a known-table recomputation nor a simple substitution in the two-cycle case, which cannot express variable knots or inverse length tomography. It does not claim factor-specific recovery or graph reconstruction.
